findings.text: refuse_a_released_launch formats the refusal with family id D23, which reckon/crew/refusals.py:89 registers as the plan-review-missing refusal, so format_refusal appends the resolving action 'run reckon crew review for the plan ... or dispatch --allow-unreviewed-plan' to a message about a released stranded launch. The mechanism is right and the step is named, but the operator is handed the wrong remedy; an unused or aptly-worded code would say 'dispatch again'. refusals.py is outside the node's declared write paths, so the registry could not be extended here.

assert record["run_id"] == RUN_ID compares the returned run id against the same RUN_ID the test passed into dispatch, so both sides move together and it cannot fail unless dispatch ignores its own input. The durability of the node does not rest on it (the holder, step and release assertions are independent readings of records production code wrote), but it is a tautology counted among the added assertions.
